header.tag_why: Halima rejected our tiered response-time pitch as "a queue with a faster timer" and asked for a named person and an on-sale plan, so the deciding gap was support coverage, not the value case.

evidence.excerpt: payments started failing about four minutes in.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Their provider's support was a ticket form.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The CEO was getting screenshots on social.
evidence.label: fact

trigger.insight: The trigger was a payment failure during a public ticket on-sale, but the real pain was slow incumbent support that answered after the sale ended. Failures had happened twice before without a replacement decision (E6, E7), so the CEO's first-hand exposure is what made it a priority.
trigger.messaging: Open with the on-sale minute-four scenario and who responds in that window, instead of general uptime or growth claims (M1, M4).

evidence.excerpt: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Ben wanted us.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: So Monday morning the COO, Halima, says they're replacing payments before the spring on-sales.
evidence.label: fact

decider.insight: Halima made the decision alone in a single meeting, and our champion Ben could not carry it. The rep never reports a second conversation with Halima, so our case reached her once and was judged on the "who" question, not on the technical wins Ben had.
decider.messaging: Give champions a short on-sale plan with named people they can take to a COO-level meeting, since that decision is made in one sitting (M5, M8).

evidence.excerpt: A named solutions engineer and an account lead, in the room.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: they said there'd be a shared channel and someone on call for every major on-sale.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I think they over-promised.
evidence.label: opinion

competitor.insight: The competitor won on named people and a specific on-sale coverage promise, which the customer heard directly from them. The rep's over-promise theory is unverified opinion, and it does not explain why Halima found their offer more credible than ours.
competitor.messaging: Match the competitor's concrete on-sale commitment with our own named coverage model rather than arguing that their promise is unrealistic.

evidence.excerpt: good.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: so it's a queue with a faster timer.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
evidence.label: quote

message.insight: The load test and uptime history got a one-word reaction, while the support-tier walkthrough was called a queue with a faster timer. The rep's view that we were "the better platform" is opinion, and Halima's own words contradict it on the criteria that mattered to her.
message.messaging: Retire tiered response times as the support story (M5) and lead with what happens to a named person when a sale goes down at minute four, not with uptime.

evidence.excerpt: so it's a queue with a faster timer.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: That sentence.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Ben had basically told his team to start planning the integration.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The rep points to Halima's remark as the moment of loss, but the rep also believed the load test had won and did not build the on-sale plan that was available. The turn was earlier and avoidable: we were in a strong position with Ben, and the rep let the "who" question go unanswered until it was too late.
decided.messaging: Put the on-sale morning plan in the first meeting, so the "queue" objection cannot surface for the first time at the close (M5, M2).

evidence.excerpt: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We don't have that as a thing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I could have built something with our solutions engineer, and I didn't.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I had logos. I didn't have a person.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The buyer asked for a written on-sale runbook and a named reference, and we had neither. The rep admits the runbook was buildable with our own solutions engineer and was not built because of confidence in the load test, which the customer did not share.
gaps.messaging: Create an on-sale morning runbook and a named ticketing reference customer who will take a buyer's call, and make both standard in our sales kit (M8).

evidence.excerpt: A name, not a queue.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Someone who picks up.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Nobody said "support." They said "who."
evidence.label: fact

language.insight: The buyer's vocabulary is about a person and a moment: a name, on-sale morning, someone who picks up. The word "support" never came up, so our support-plan framing sits outside their frame. The speaker of "A name, not a queue." is not identified in the transcript, so attribution should be confirmed before reuse.
language.messaging: Replace "support plans" and "tiered response times" in M5 with "a named person on every on-sale," using the buyer's own words.

gaps.question: Which vendor won, and what on-sale coverage did they commit to?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Ben (CTO) directly which vendor was chosen and what they promised for on-sale mornings.

gaps.question: Why was the on-sale plan not built, given the solutions engineer was available?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Jordan (rep) what stopped them from building the on-sale plan with our solutions engineer before the COO meeting.

gaps.question: Did Halima hear the competitor's specific on-sale promise, and did she ask us about it?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Ben whether the competitor's on-call commitment came up in the room with Halima.

gaps.question: Is the replacement partial, covering only online or only some markets, or is the whole payments stack moving?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Ben whether in-store and online payments are both moving before the spring on-sales.

gaps.question: Who said "A name, not a queue." and "Someone who picks up."?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Ben whether those phrases came from him, Halima, or another member of their team.

gaps.question: Is the rep's claim that we were the better platform supported by anything the customer said?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Jordan (rep) for any customer statement, outside the load test, that supports the better-platform view.

close.rep_takeaway: The load test made you confident, but the buyer's question was "who picks up at minute four" and you answered with a tier table. Before any support slide, build the on-sale morning plan with your solutions engineer and ask the buyer who they would call at minute four.
